newsitem.title: UK: LPC - Merrill in $1.5 bln credit deal for Atlas.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Merrill in $1.5 bln credit deal for Atlas.

text.p: LONDON, June 11 (LPC) - Merril Lynch is arranging a $1.5 billion multicurrency revolving credit for Swedish engineering company Atlas Copco, which will back the company's $900 million agreed takeover bid for U.S. machine leasing company Prime Service Inc, market sources said. The deal is one of the largest acquisition facilities to be arranged for a Scandinavian borrower.

Pricing on the five-year credit is tied to a ratings grid, and the company will pay a starting margin of 20 bps over LIBOR with a commitment fee of 7.5 bps, and the price will be adjusted once the company is rated.

The credit will support an increase in Atlas' commercial paper programme and refinance the debt of both companies. Atlas has an outstanding $250 million seven-year revolving credit, which was arranged by Enskilda in February 1995, and is priced at 20 bps for years one to five, rising to 25 bps for years six and seven. Prime Services also has $260 million of debt outstanding.
Merrill Lynch is currently looking to appoint an administrative agent for the deal and a bank meeting will be held in London on June 18.

The deal is the second large transatlantic acquisition facility that Merrill has arranged this year - the bank also financed American Electric Power and Public Service Co of Colorado's 1.5 billion stg acquisition of Yorkshire Electricity plc in May. The new mandate is a further example of the one-stop shopping philosophy pioneered by U.S. investment banks, as Merrill also acted as Atlas' advisor.

The ratings agencies reacted quickly to the announcement - Moody's put Atlas under review for a possible downgrade and S&P put the company on creditwatch, as the deal, which is Atlas' largest acquisition, is almost entirely debt financed.
